text.p: H.F. Ahmanson and Co Chief Executive Charles Rinehart on Thursday said he expected pressure from shareholders of Great Western Financial Corp to intensify over the next week and potentially force Great Western's board to negotiate with Ahmanson.
"Ultimately, the market votes in this deal. The next week and a half could definitely create a circumstance where Great Western's board will allow us to talk," Rinehart told Reuters.

Rinehart was referring to a revised consent solicitation sent to Great Western shareholders on Wednesday asking them to support proposals to treat all bidders equally, negotiate with Ahmanson and to set an annual meeting date. Ahmanson has asked the shareholders to return the consent cards by March 27.
"The consent gives us the ability to put these issues (on the agenda) at the shareholder annual meeting," Rinehart said.
Rinehart declined to say whether Ahmanson would raise its bid if rival suitor Washington Mutual Inc revised its friendly offer.
"Based on what we heard from analysts and so on, nobody believes that Washington Mutual has the capacity to go any higher," Rinehart said.

"They're stretched awfully hard with their assumptions and analysis to get to this bid," he said. "That doesn't mean they won't. Who knows what they may try to do, but I think it would be a real stretch, so at this point we expect that the bids will probably stay where they are."

Ahmanson this week raised its all-stock hostile tender offer for Great Western to at least 1.10 shares for each Great Western share. On March 6, Great Western signed a definitive agreement to be acquired by Washington Mutual. Great Western has said it will study Ahmanson's revised bid, but has not yet offered to open discussions with Ahmanson.
"To the extent they continue to say nothing, the consent solicitation will certainly help to demonstrate what the shareholders are thinking," Rinehart said.
"Our primary hope is that the Great Western board will decide to let us come in and negotiate and evaluate as they did with Washington Mutual," he said.
"Ultimately, if the shareholders decide they like us better, it will put pressure on Great Western," he said.
Rinehart said if the two thrifts did not meet at the table, he thought the final decision on the merger would come down to shareholders at the annual meeting.
He said it would take several days before Ahmanson started to get the consent cards back in significant numbers.
Rinehart spoke to Reuters in an interview before a news conference announcing a $70 billion community reinvestment commitment over 10 years by Ahmanson's Home Savings Bank.

Home Savings made the pledge assuming completion of the merger with Great Western. Rinehart said at the news conference that if the proposed merger dod not go through, the pledge would fall to about half that amount.
